backlog.spec: Instead of independent random restarts, use the best packing found so far as the initial guess for the next SLSQP run, adding a small amount of random jitter to avoid local minima.
backlog.title: Multi-Start SLSQP with Warm Start

backlog.spec: Instead of a uniform INIT_RADIUS, initialize radii using a power-law or a weighted distribution (e.g., some large, some small) to explore different packing structures.
backlog.title: Variable Radii Initialization

backlog.spec: In the repair function, if a circle overlaps with multiple others, distribute the shrinkage proportionally to the magnitude of the overlap for all involved circles.
backlog.title: Dynamic Shrinkage Repair

backlog.spec: Replace the hard constraints in SLSQP with a penalty method (e.g., adding a high penalty for overlaps and boundary violations to the objective function) to allow the solver to traverse infeasible regions.
backlog.title: Penalty Method Alternative

backlog.spec: Initialize all radii to a very small value and use a loop to incrementally increase them (or use SLSQP to maximize them) while keeping the packing valid.
backlog.title: Sequential Radius Expansion

backlog.spec: Scale MAX_ITER based on the remaining time in the `solve` loop, giving more iterations to promising packings that are close to the boundary of the feasible region.
backlog.title: Adaptive Max Iterations

backlog.spec: Implement a simple SGD or Adam-style optimizer where the gradient of the sum of radii is calculated with respect to centers and radii, using a penalty for overlaps.
backlog.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)

backlog.spec: Sort the circles by radius (descending) during initialization and repair. This can help in prioritizing the placement of larger circles which are harder to fit.
backlog.title: Pre-sorting Circles

backlog.spec: After a repair, perform a local search by slightly perturbing the centers of circles that are in 'tight' spots (distance between edges < epsilon) and re-running a few iterations of SLSQP.
backlog.title: Iterative Local Search

backlog.spec: In the repair step, instead of just shrinking, if a circle is pushed outside the boundary, reflect its center back into the unit square.
backlog.title: Bouncing Repair

backlog.spec: Modify the objective function to maximize the sum of radii while also maximizing the minimum distance between any two circles (to 'loosen' the packing) before doing a final expansion.
backlog.title: Multi-Objective Objective

backlog.spec: Instead of purely random centers, use a greedy approach to place circles one by one (largest first) into the first available spot that doesn't overlap, then use this as the starting point for SLSQP.
backlog.title: Greedy Seed Initialization

backlog.spec: Replace SLSQP with a Simulated Annealing approach where the energy function is the negative sum of radii plus a large penalty for overlaps.
backlog.title: Simulated Annealing

backlog.spec: Use the `scipy.optimize.minimize` with the `L-BFGS-B` method by converting constraints into bounds (difficult for overlaps) or use a trust-region approach if possible.
backlog.title: Trust Region Method

backlog.spec: In the repair step, if a packing is invalid, apply a small random displacement to the centers of the overlapping circles until the overlap is resolved.
backlog.title: Random Walk Repair

backlog.spec: Fix the centers of the largest 10 circles and solve for the remaining 16. Then rotate the 'largest' set and repeat, keeping the best overall.
backlog.title: Nested Solve

backlog.spec: Simulate the circles as particles with 'growing' radii and repulsive forces. Let them settle into a steady state, then use the result as an SLSQP starting point.
backlog.title: Velocity-based Physics

backlog.spec: Treat circles as having 'soft' boundaries where overlap costs a quadratic penalty. Use SLSQP to minimize the cost of overlap while maximizing radii.
backlog.title: Elastic Band Model

backlog.spec: In the repair function, instead of 50 fixed iterations, continue until all overlaps are less than 1e-11, using a smaller shrinking factor to maintain more area.
backlog.title: Better Repair Loop

backlog.spec: Start with all radii = 0.01 and slowly increase them by a small delta in each step, re-running the optimizer/repair at each step.
backlog.title: Gradual Radius Scaling

backlog.spec: After the repair step, add a very small amount of Gaussian noise to the centers and re-run the repair/optimizer to see if the packing can 'settle' into a better state.
backlog.title: Center Jittering

backlog.spec: Use a large slack variable for the overlap constraints in SLSQP, and then use a two-stage optimization to drive the slack to zero.
backlog.title: Constraint Relaxation

backlog.spec: Use a quasi-random sequence (like a Sobol sequence, if we can approximate it with a few PRNG calls) for initial centers to ensure better coverage of the unit square.
backlog.title: Sobol Sequence

backlog.spec: Sample radii from a distribution where the sum of radii is guaranteed to be slightly less than the maximum possible sum (e.g., a Gaussian centered around a target sum).
backlog.title: Circle Size Distribution

backlog.spec: If time allows, run multiple `_solve_once` calls in parallel (though the limit is one thread, we can still structure the code to process a 'batch' of restarts efficiently).
backlog.title: Parallel Restart

backlog.spec: After SLSQP finishes, perform a few hundred iterations of a manual gradient descent step on the radii, calculating the gradient by checking which circles are 'touching'.
backlog.title: Local Gradient Descent

backlog.spec: Change the constraint `1 - c[:, 0] - r` to `1 - c[:, 0] - r + 1e-11` to give the solver a tiny bit of 'breathing room' before the final repair.
backlog.title: Refined Boundary Constraint

backlog.spec: In the repair step, if a circle is overlapping many others, shrink its radius to the average of the distances to its neighbors.
backlog.title: Shrink to Mean

backlog.spec: Perform the first `_solve_once` with a fixed, known 'good' layout (like a grid), then use random restarts for the rest of the time.
backlog.title: Initial Guess Perturbation

backlog.spec: If `_solve_once` returns a result that is significantly worse than the current best, immediately discard it and restart with a different seed without completing the full time slice.
backlog.title: Heuristic Restart

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform random centers, generate a hexagonal grid of circles with a large initial radius. Randomly shift the grid slightly and vary the radii of the circles to create a high-density starting point. This provides a much better structured initial guess than uniform randomness.
backlog.title: Hexagonal Grid Initialization

backlog.spec: Implement a simple physics-based simulation where circles are treated as hard bodies with initial velocities. Use a repulsion force to resolve overlaps and a 'growth' pressure to increase radii. Run this for a fixed number of steps before passing the result to SLSQP.
backlog.title: Velocity-based Physics (Particle Relaxation)

backlog.spec: Start with small radii such that no circles overlap. Iteratively increase the radii of the circles (perhaps prioritizing smaller ones to maintain balance) while using a gradient descent step on the centers to resolve new overlaps until no more expansion is possible.
backlog.title: Sequential Radius Expansion

backlog.spec: Replace the linear shrinkage in the repair step with a 'bouncing' logic: if two circles overlap, move them apart along the vector connecting their centers until they just touch, rather than just shrinking their radii. This preserves more area per iteration.
backlog.title: Bouncing Repair

backlog.spec: Redefine the objective function to include a large penalty for overlaps: f(v) = -sum(r) + lambda * sum(max(0, overlap_dist)^2). Use a high lambda and perform several warm-starts with increasing lambda values to strictly enforce the constraints.
backlog.title: Penalty Method with Logarithmic Barrier

backlog.spec: Divide the problem into two stages. First, use a fast local optimizer (like a limited-step SLSQP) to find a valid packing of circles with a fixed set of radii. Second, use a second SLSQP to optimize the radii and centers simultaneously, starting from the first stage's result.
backlog.title: Nested Solve (Two-Stage Optimization)

backlog.spec: Dynamically adjust the MAX_ITER parameter based on the progress of the current SLSQP run. If the change in the sum of radii is very small over 10 iterations, terminate early to save time for more restarts.
backlog.title: Adaptive Max Iterations

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform initial radii, sample the initial radii from a power-law or non-uniform distribution. Often, a mix of very large 'anchor' circles and many smaller 'filler' circles leads to higher packing density.
backlog.title: Circle Size Distribution (Power Law)

backlog.spec: Model the circles as elastic bodies connected by springs to their neighbors (if they overlap). Minimize the total energy of the system, where energy is a combination of the negative sum of radii and the 'compression' energy of overlaps. Slowly 'harden' the springs over time.
backlog.title: Soft-Body Elastic Model

backlog.spec: Place the largest possible circles one by one into the square using a greedy approach (place the next circle in the spot that minimizes the distance to the nearest boundary/circle). Use this resulting packing as the starting point for the SLSQP solver.
backlog.title: Greedy Seed Initialization

backlog.spec: Instead of hard constraints in SLSQP, reformulate the objective as minimizing -sum(radii) + kappa * sum(log(barrier_functions)). The barrier functions would ensure circles stay within [0, 1] and maintain distance from each other. Gradually increase kappa (continuation method) to push the solution towards the feasible boundary.
backlog.title: Logarithmic Barrier Penalties

backlog.spec: Replace one of the SLSQP restarts with an SGLD step. Use the gradient of the overlap energy and add a small amount of Gaussian noise to the update. This helps the solver escape local optima that SLSQP (a local solver) might get stuck in, while still maintaining a gradient-based trajectory.
backlog.title: Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD)

backlog.spec: Instead of a soft-body relaxation for initialization, use a greedy approach: place circles one by one from largest to smallest in the 'best' available location (point of maximum distance from existing edges/circles). Use this layout as the starting point for the soft-body relaxation or SLSQP.
backlog.title: Hierarchical Greedy Packing Seed

backlog.spec: Implement a multi-stage optimization where radii are initialized very small (nearly zero). In each stage, increase the radii by a small factor and run a few iterations of SLSQP to find a valid configuration. This 'growth' schedule helps the circles find a packed configuration without getting tangled in early high-overlap states.
backlog.title: Dynamic Radius Growth Schedule

backlog.spec: Identify the circles that are 'most constrained' (e.g., those with the smallest remaining room or highest overlap). Fix their centers in place for a few iterations while optimizing the radii and centers of the remaining 'free' circles, then rotate the set of 'pinned' circles.
backlog.title: Active Set Circle Pinning

backlog.spec: Modify the repair loop to include a momentum term. Instead of shrinking radii based only on the current maximum overlap, maintain a velocity vector for each radius's shrinkage rate. This helps smooth out the repair process and prevents oscillations in high-density clusters.
backlog.title: Momentum-based Repair

backlog.spec: Add a high-magnitude penalty term to the objective function: Energy = -sum(r) + lambda * sum(max(0, overlap)^2). Use a very large lambda (e.g., 1e6) and a larger MAX_ITER for SLSQP. This converts the constrained problem into an unconstrained-style problem which SLSQP can sometimes navigate more fluidly.
backlog.title: Over-constrained Penalty Method

backlog.spec: Modify the initial soft-body relaxation to include a small entropy term that encourages circles to be spread out evenly before the radius expansion/hardening phase begins. This prevents early 'clumping' that can create non-convex local optima.
backlog.title: Entropy-Regularized Initialization

backlog.spec: Combine SLSQP and Simulated Annealing. Use SLSQP to perform local optimization to find a local optimum, then apply a 'jump' (Metropolis-Hastings move) by slightly jittering all centers and radii. If the new packing is valid and better (or meets the Boltzmann criterion), keep it.
backlog.title: Simulated Annealing with SLSQP Steps

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform radii, sample initial radii from a power-law distribution (e.g., f(r) → r−ḻ). Smaller circles are much more likely and can fill the interstices between larger circles more efficiently, potentially leading to a higher total sum.
backlog.title: Circle Size Power-Law Distribution

backlog.spec: Modify _solve_once to use a two-stage approach. First, solve the packing with very small radii (e.g., 0.01) using the current SLSQP method to find a valid configuration. Then, gradually increase all radii by a factor (e.g., 1.1x) and re-run a few iterations of SLSQP or a local gradient step to 'inflate' the circles until they hit each other or the boundaries. This helps avoid getting stuck in local optima where large circles block small ones early on.
backlog.title: Iterative Radius Growth (Sequential Expansion)

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform distribution of initial radii in _soft_relax with a power-law distribution. Specifically, sample radii from a distribution where larger radii are rarer (e.g., 0.01 + 0.1 * (random_val**0.5)). This is often more efficient for packing problems because it prevents the solver from wasting time trying to pack many equally-sized large circles first.
backlog.title: Power-Law Radii Distribution

backlog.spec: Introduce a callback or a check inside the SLSQP call in _solve_once. If the change in the sum of radii becomes smaller than 1e-6 over 50 iterations, terminate the solver early. This allows the script to move on to the next random restart faster, potentially exploring more configurations in the same time limit.
backlog.title: Early SLSQP Termination with Radius Check

backlog.spec: Modify the SLSQP step to 'pin' the centers of the $k$ largest circles (e.g., $k=5$). Pinning means their positions are held constant while the solver optimizes the centers of the remaining smaller circles and the radii of all circles. This reduces the degrees of freedom and can prevent large circles from being pushed into inefficient positions by smaller ones.
backlog.title: Active Set Circle Pinning

backlog.spec: Update the _repair function to include a momentum term for radius shrinkage. Instead of just shrinking $r[i]$ and $r[j]$ by a factor $s$, maintain a 'velocity' for each radius that determines how much it shrinks in each iteration. This can help the repair loop smooth out the adjustments when multiple circles are overlapping simultaneously.
backlog.title: Momentum-based Repair

backlog.spec: Add a log-barrier penalty term to the objective function in _soft_relax specifically for the boundary constraints. Instead of just $k(a^2 + b^2)$, use $k 	imes 	ext{log}(	ext{distance to wall})$. This creates a 'repulsion' from the walls that gets stronger as circles approach the edge, potentially leading to better-centered packed structures.
backlog.title: Logarithmic Barrier Penalty for Walls

backlog.spec: Replace the hard constraints in SLSQP with a soft penalty. Define the objective as $- 	ext{sum}(r) + 	ext{penalty} 	imes 	ext{overlap}$. Start with a small penalty and gradually increase it to a very large value (e.g., $10^6$) over the course of the SLSQP iterations. This 'anneals' the constraints into being hard boundaries.
backlog.title: Dynamic Slack Relaxation

backlog.spec: Modify _soft_relax to start with a greedy packing of the largest circles (placed one by one at the first available spot) and then treat that configuration as the initial state for the soft-body relaxation. This combines the benefits of a good heuristic with the local optimization of the soft-body model.
backlog.title: Greedy-to-Soft Hybrid Initialization

backlog.spec: Modify the objective function to be a weighted sum of the sum of radii and the sum of the squares of the radii (proportional to area). By including a small weight for the area ($	ext{sum}(r_i^2)$), the solver may favor more 'balanced' packings that are less likely to be trapped in configurations where a few large circles are poorly placed.
backlog.title: Multi-Objective Sum of Radii and Area

backlog.spec: Modify the _repair function so that if a circle's center is pushed outside the [0, 1] range due to overlap resolution, it is 'reflected' back into the unit square (like a billiard ball) rather than being clipped. This maintains the momentum of the adjustment and can explore more valid configurations in the repair step.
backlog.title: Bouncing Repair Boundaries

backlog.spec: Instead of initializing radii uniformly or with a fixed small constant, sample the initial radii from a power-law distribution (e.g., $f(r) \propto r^{-\alpha}$). This is motivated by the observation that packing problems often yield optimal results with a diverse range of circle sizes, with many small circles filling the gaps between larger ones. Use a distribution that favors smaller radii but allows for a few large 'anchor' circles.
backlog.title: Power-Law Radius Distribution

backlog.spec: In the `_solve_once` function, implement a callback or a manual check within the SLSQP loop. If the sum of radii has not improved by more than a tiny epsilon (e.g., 1e-7) over the last 50 iterations, terminate the current SLSQP call early and move to the repair step. This frees up time for more restarts.
backlog.title: Early Exit via Radius Sum Change

backlog.spec: Modify the `_repair` function to include a 'momentum' term. When shrinking radii to resolve an overlap, maintain a velocity vector for each radius. In subsequent iterations, the shrinkage amount is influenced by the previous shrinkage direction, helping to resolve 'oscillating' overlaps where two circles are pushed back and forth by multiple neighbors.
backlog.title: Momentum-based Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of initializing with large radii and shrinking, start all radii at a very small value (e.g., 0.005) with a valid packing. Gradually increase all radii by a small delta $\Delta r$ in a loop. In each step, use a quick local optimizer or the repair step to re-establish feasibility. Continue until the packing is no longer feasible.
backlog.title: Sequential Radius Expansion

backlog.spec: Modify the `_soft_relax` energy function to include a logarithmic barrier term: $E = -\sum r_i + \sum \log(c_{i,x} - r_i) + \sum \log(c_{i,y} - r_i) + \sum \log(1 - c_{i,x} - r_i) + \sum \log(1 - c_{i,y} - r_i)$. This pushes circles away from the boundaries more aggressively during the soft-body relaxation phase.
backlog.title: Logarithmic Barrier Penalties for Walls

backlog.spec: In the `_repair` function, if a circle's radius is shrunk such that it would move out of bounds, or if a center is moved out of bounds during the repair process, 'reflect' the coordinate or the radius change back into the interior. This prevents the repair step from creating invalid configurations that the harness would crash on.
backlog.title: Bouncing Repair Boundaries

backlog.spec: Add an entropy-like term to the `_soft_relax` energy: $E = -\sum r_i + k_1\sum(overlaps) + k_2\sum(boundary) - k_3 \sum 	ext{Var}(r_i)$. This encourages a diverse distribution of radii, preventing the relaxation from collapsing into a state where all circles have nearly identical small radii.
backlog.title: Entropy-Regularized Initialization

backlog.spec: Start the `_soft_relax` phase by first performing a quick greedy packing (place circles one by one at the first available position that doesn't overlap). Then, use the coordinates of this greedy packing as the starting point for the soft-body relaxation. This provides a much higher-quality starting point than a random layout.
backlog.title: Greedy-to-Soft Hybrid Initialization

incumbent.description: Replace the uniform random initial layout with a soft-body relaxation: circles are treated as springs that penalise overlap and wall contact, minimised with L-BFGS-B while the spring stiffness is hardened over four stages, and the result seeds the existing SLSQP polish.

memo: Helped: better initial layouts. Slot 10 (soft-body relaxation init) is the only accept: -2.6321/-2.6297 over 2 runs, delta -0.0029, incumbent -2.6309. Mild gains, all single runs and within noise (sd 0.0023): gradual radius scaling (-2.6329), early SLSQP abort (-2.6327), square-grid first restart (-2.6327), log-distance repulsion (-2.6327), area term (-2.6327), iterative radius growth (-2.6321). Power-law radii gave -2.6301/-2.6303. Did not help: Sobol init, post-repair jitter/local search, slack penalty, warm-start from best (+0.0060), nested solve, greedy init (+0.0107), Adam-style relaxation, annealing polish, shifted-grid init. Many aborts were repeats of rejected ideas, so check the table first. Next: replicate the -2.6327 and -2.6329 candidates, then combine the ones that hold up (early abort, gradual radius scaling, power-law radii). Tune soft-body steps and radius scale. The gap to 2.6360 is about 0.005. Avoid changes that reduce diversity.
